title: Core concepts
text: One workspace holds your data. The app calls each working record an Entry; projects can group Entries, Entries contain ordered sequence blocks, and blocks carry features. The CLI and MCP retain the underlying conversation term for an Entry so existing automation contracts stay stable. Screenshots and recordings show the direct edition. Compare editions . The workspace hierarchy One SQLite database holds the workspace. Projects group Entries, an Entry holds an ordered list of blocks, and each block carries features. headings: Paste or drag in the desktop app
Native Save As in the desktop app
text: Read eleven formats, write FASTA, GenBank, and GFF3. Bring sequences into your workspace by file, paste, or drag, and write them back out from the CLI or the desktop app. SEAL reads and writes three sequence formats. The parser detects the format from the file contents, so you do not pass a format flag on import. Auto-detection keys off the file contents: a FASTA > header, a GenBank LOCUS line, or a GFF3 ##gff-version 3 directive. A file with multiple > headers or multiple LOCUS blocks is a multi-record file, and import splits it into one block per record. FASTA records hold sequence only. To

title: Agent control plane
text: External agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI read and write the same local workspace you use by hand. They connect over MCP, use explicit tools, and record each write in Activity. This guide covers source and direct-edition tools. These tools are not bundled with the first Store release. Compare editions . The agent control loop The agent calls an MCP tool, the tool reads from and writes to the SQLite workspace, the write is recorded in Activity, and the agent reads that record back to confirm the change. title: Privacy
headings: Direct and source editions: local data
text: SEAL is local-first. Workspace data stays on your device unless you explicitly start a network-backed fetch, prediction, hosted-model request, source-edition Notion diagnostic, or external-agent action. SEAL sends no background telemetry, analytics, or crash reports. The first Store configuration uses sandbox-managed default storage and user-selected workspace folders. It does not enable terminal launching, external tool runtimes, or hosted-provider credential storage. See the Store privacy summary and Edition differences .
